# `cron_job`

A scheduled job is a command that a node runs by itself at set times, such
as a nightly cleanup. `cron_job` manages one cron entry in its own file,
`/etc/cron.d/<name>`, on the node. `cron_job` is for teams that keep
their schedules in cron.

For new jobs, use [`systemd_scheduled_job`](systemd_scheduled_job.md)
instead. With it, a job has a multi-line script with the same rules as
`shell`, secrets stay out of world-readable files, two runs never overlap, a
missed run can be made up after downtime, output is in the journal instead
of mail, and `systemctl list-timers` shows the next run.

## Set up

cron must be installed and running on the node. The package
`cron` provides cron on Debian and Ubuntu and `cronie` on the Red Hat family. The `cron_job` module installs no package and
starts no service, so put the package node task and the service node task
first:

```yaml
- when: {equals: ["{{ .node.package_manager }}", apt]}
  apt_package: {packages: [{name: cron, version: newest_when_first_installed}]}
- when: {equals: ["{{ .node.package_manager }}", apt]}
  systemd_service: {name: cron, start_at_boot: true, state: running}

- when: {equals: ["{{ .node.package_manager }}", dnf]}
  dnf_package: {packages: [{name: cronie, version: newest_when_first_installed}]}
- when: {equals: ["{{ .node.package_manager }}", dnf]}
  systemd_service: {name: crond, start_at_boot: true, state: running}
```

The service is `cron` on Debian and Ubuntu, and `crond` on the Red Hat
family.

## Inputs

- `name` (string; required): the file's name: letters, digits, - and _ only, because cron ignores other file names
- `cron_schedule` (string; required): five cron fields (minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week), such as `"15 3 * * *"`, or one of cron's @ words: @reboot, @yearly, @annually, @monthly, @weekly, @daily, @midnight, @hourly
- `run_as_user_account` (string; required): the account cron runs the command as; cron needs it on every entry in /etc/cron.d
- `command` (string; required): one line, run by cron with /bin/sh; write % as it should reach the command, MMX escapes it for cron
- `env` (mapping; optional): variable lines written above the entry, such as MAILTO or PATH; a secret is rejected, because every account can read the file
- `state` (`present` or `absent`; default `present`): absent accepts only name and state; it removes a file that has MMX's marker line and refuses one that lacks it

## Outputs

The node task's result holds these fields. A later node task reads them as `.node_tasks.<id>.<field>`, where `<id>` is the node task's `id`.

- `status`
- `change`

## What a dryrun reports

Supported; shows the file's text difference; a node without cron is not checked.

## Retries and time limits

Bounded automatic retries by default; retry: false turns them off.

The node task takes the time limits `time_limit` and `time_limit_per_try`; without them, the project's `node_task_defaults` apply. `mmx describe-module task` describes the settings every node task accepts.

## Examples

### Keep a job in cron

```yaml
- cron_job:
    name: rotate-upload-cache
    cron_schedule: "15 3 * * *"
    run_as_user_account: www-data
    command: /usr/local/bin/rotate-upload-cache --keep 14 --suffix $(date +%Y-%m-%d)
    env:
      MAILTO: ops@example.com
```

MMX writes the file `/etc/cron.d/rotate-upload-cache` on the node, owned by
root with mode `0644`:

```text
# Managed by MMX: cron_job. Written by the node task for rotate-upload-cache; MMX replaces a change made here on its next run.
MAILTO=ops@example.com
15 3 * * * www-data /usr/local/bin/rotate-upload-cache --keep 14 --suffix $(date +\%Y-\%m-\%d)
```

At 03:15 every night, cron runs the command with `/bin/sh` as the account
`www-data`. cron reads a `%` in a command as the end of the command, so MMX
writes each `%` as `\%`; write the command as it should reach the shell.

## How it works

- `name` is the file's name in `/etc/cron.d/`: letters, digits, `-`, and `_`
  only, because cron ignores other file names.
- `cron_schedule` is five cron fields, or one of cron's `@` words:
  `@reboot`, `@yearly`, `@annually`, `@monthly`, `@weekly`, `@daily`,
  `@midnight`, or `@hourly`.
- `run_as_user_account` is required, because cron needs the account on
  every entry in `/etc/cron.d/`.
- `command` is one line, and runs as written: MMX fills in no reference
  there, and validation refuses one to a value MMX knows, such as
  `cd {{ .inputs.sites_dir }}`, which cron would run with its braces.
  Put the value in `env`, such as `env: {SITES_DIR: "{{ .inputs.sites_dir }}"}`,
  and write `cd "$SITES_DIR"` in the command.
- `env` holds variable lines written above the entry, such as `MAILTO` or
  `PATH`.
- The file is written like a [`file`](file.md) node task: MMX compares it
  with what the node task asks for, writes it only when it differs, and
  shows the text difference in a dryrun. In a node task block's `changes`,
  the file is a tracked input, like a file from a `file` node task.
- `state: absent` removes the file when it starts with MMX's marker line,
  and refuses a file without it, because then MMX did not write it.
- A present job also refuses, in a dryrun and in a run, an existing file of
  that name without the marker line, such as a package's own
  `/etc/cron.d/certbot`. Choose another `name`.

## Errors and what they mean

| The reason holds | What the error means, and what to do |
|---|---|
| `cron is not installed; install the package that provides it in an earlier node task: cron (apt, zypper), cronie (dnf)` | Install cron in an earlier node task; see [Set up](#set-up). A dryrun reports the node task not checked, because an earlier node task may install cron. A missing `run_as_user_account` account is treated the same way. |
| `a secret cannot go into a cron file, which every account on the node can read; use systemd_scheduled_job, which keeps a secret in a file only root can read` | Every account on the node can read the file. Use [`systemd_scheduled_job`](systemd_scheduled_job.md) for a job that needs a secret. |
| `cron_job.command must not have a backslash directly before %: cron cannot pass that pair to a command. Write the % without the backslash; MMX escapes every % for cron` | cron has no way to pass that pair to a command. |
| `refusing to write /etc/cron.d/...: the file exists and lacks the MMX marker line ...` | A file of that name that MMX did not write exists, and the job would overwrite it. Choose another `name`. |
| `refusing to remove /etc/cron.d/...: the file lacks the MMX marker line ...` | Another tool or a person wrote the file. Remove it by hand, or with a `file` node task (`state: absent`). |

## Tested on

**Distributions:** Debian 12 and 13, Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04, Rocky Linux 9, AlmaLinux 10.

The suite `tests/integration/scheduled_jobs.py` runs on Debian 12 and 13, Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04, Rocky Linux 9, and AlmaLinux 10, in containers on the first four and in virtual machines on the last two. It checks
the cron file and cron running the
entry; on a node without cron, it checks the dryrun and the failure that
names the package. The [validation record](../../changing-mmx/validation.md) has the
latest results.

## Why it works this way

- **`cron_job` is a core module beside `systemd_scheduled_job`.** Each is
  named for its tool, and many teams have cron entries they do not want to
  convert yet.
- **No secrets in `env`.** The file in `/etc/cron.d/` is readable by every
  account.
